entryAnswer.explanation:
What the adapter does. `mountSpendingAlertsDisplay` takes an already-created `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback, subscribes to the view's five business ports (`assessment`, `publication`, `coverage`, `issues`, `startup`), and renders the current available values together with an explicit `unavailable` list. It creates no instance, no input facts and no business state; it only observes the original view (README.md:34, causal-view-binding.ts:1-2).

Ports and values. The view is exactly the frozen object built in causal-preset.ts:171-177 (`assessment`, `publication`, `coverage`, `issues`, `startup`), and `SpendingAlertsView` is its type (causal-preset.ts:206). Each port is a `Node<T>`, so `ValueOf` extracts the payload type (causal-view-binding.ts:5-8).

Current values, not a snapshot. `Node.subscribe` is push-on-subscribe: a new sink receives `START`, then cached `DATA` (or `DIRTY` if dirty) (node.ts:416-419, 445-458). The adapter therefore renders the latest value per port, which is explicitly not an atomic multi-port snapshot and not independent evidence (causal-view-binding.ts:9-13; README.md:142).

Unavailable ports. A port is reported unavailable when it has no current usable value: it never delivered `DATA`, or it delivered `INVALIDATE`/`ERROR`. On `INVALIDATE` the node clears its cache to SENTINEL, drops `hasData`, empties the replay ring and broadcasts `INVALIDATE` (node-output-runtime.ts:451-459); `ERROR` is a terminal that also ends value output (node-output-runtime.ts:195-201). The adapter deletes the stored value on both, so a stale displayed value is never retained (README.md:138). `START`, `DIRTY`, `RESOLVED`, `COMPLETE` and `TEARDOWN` carry no new usable value and are ignored for value purposes.

Cleanup. The returned function ends observation only: it unsubscribes every port subscription (reverse order, idempotent) and stops rendering. Unsubscribing the last sink deactivates the node (node.ts:441-444), but run ownership stays with the application (causal-view-binding.ts:16).

What "a value becoming unavailable" means. It means that port has no current usable fact; the old value must not be kept on screen (README.md:138). It is a per-port observation, not a statement that the run ended: business stop, node `COMPLETE` and run termination are distinct, and the protocol has no END message (README.md:153-157).

What "unmounting" means. Unmounting stops observation; the running instance keeps its outstanding obligations, retained request/admission/outcome records and bounded retention (README.md:143, 146-151). Panel cleanup is not recovery and does not close the instance, release the resource or prove normal lifecycle completion (README.md:144, 156-157).

Scope limits. The adapter does not poll diagnostics, does not claim the whole run ended, and does not treat readiness flags as proof of termination or resource release (README.md:144, 153). It also does not use the public `subscribeNodeValues` adapter, which ignores `INVALIDATE` and is not a substitute for this view contract (README.md:159-161). No code was executed.
